title: Dez Cadeiras: Ten Chairs, Ten Kairos Counter-Strike Players
subtitle: A Dust2.us roster feature with all ten Kairos Main and Academy Counter-Strike players, filmed mid-training.
summary: All ten Kairos Counter-Strike players, Main and Academy, sit for a Dust2.us feature during a training block: favorite map, one weapon forever, pre-Kairos life, and teammate banter.

content.text: This article is a fictional dramatization written for the Kairos Universe story. It is formatted in the style of a Dust2.us roster feature, but it is not an actual Dust2.us publication, video, or statement.

Following the response to Riot Games' League roster feature, Dust2.us asked to do the same for [[organization:kairos-esports|Kairos]]'s Counter-Strike side. A crew set up ten chairs, five black for [[team:kairos-cs-main|Kairos Main]] and five green for [[team:kairos-cs-academy|Kairos Academy]], in one of the campus media rooms during a scheduled training block. The session was budgeted at forty minutes; it ran well past an hour.

Kairospedia's archive entry records when this page was compiled, not a confirmed Dust2.us broadcast date — the episode that depicts the filming never states when, or whether, Dust2.us itself released the footage.

[[player:caleb-atlas-mercer|Caleb "Atlas" Mercer]], Main's IGL, named Inferno: "you can't hide behind mechanics forever — the map demands communication." His one weapon forever would be the AK. Before Counter-Strike, he played ice hockey as a defenseman and still watches the NHL every season; he also builds very large jigsaw puzzles, a thousand pieces or more, purely for the irritation of it.

[[player:owen-glacier-fletcher|Owen "Glacier" Fletcher]] picked Nuke — "especially as an AWPer," he said, pointing to how much the map rewards information, rotation, and vertical pressure over pure aim — and would keep the AWP as his only weapon. He previously worked a few hours a week at a convenience store, handling stock, the register, and cleaning, and is interested in military history, specifically strategy, logistics, and historical campaigns, not weapons or collecting.

[[player:emiliano-moteconhuesillo-navarro|Emiliano "MoteConHuesillo" Navarro]] answered Cobblestone — a map he missed after it rotated out of competitive play — while admitting with a laugh that it isn't necessarily the best map in the pool, just his favorite. His weapon would be the AK. He played futsal for years as a winger and learned to cook a range of Mexican dishes from his family.

[[player:cameron-mold-ruiz|Cameron "Mold" Ruiz]] named Dust II — "the most honest map that exists," in his words — and would keep the AK. Before Kairos, he spent time walking desert trails near home for hours, without music or a podcast, just walking. He also draws, mostly cars, buildings, and faces, though he declined to show any of it on camera.

[[player:vincente-flacogomez-galan|Vincente "FLACOGOMEZ" Galán]] closed out Main with Train — "it always feels like there's one more thing happening than you can actually see" — and the M4A1-S. He played futsal and has followed Palmeiras since childhood, and collects football shirts, by his own admission "about twenty," though teammates suspect the real number is higher.

[[player:evan-soupcrime-nakamura|Evan "RAMENSOUP" Nakamura]] picked Nuke and the AK. He did competitive debate in school and likes cooking real ramen from scratch, broth and toppings included, not instant.
[[player:milo-velcrodog-radovic|Milo "velcroDAWG" Radović]] answered Inferno and the AK. He plays basketball when he has time and speaks enough Serbian to talk with part of his family.

[[player:zayn-parkinglot-haddad|Zayn "p4rkingl0t" Haddad]] named Train and, after briefly considering the M4, settled on the AK. He likes cars, models, engines, and sounds, and can identify some cars just by how they sound; he has also done nighttime automotive photography for friends near parking lots, gas stations, and city lights.

[[player:nolan-dentalplan-hart|Nolan "dentalplan" Hart]] picked Dust II — an AWPer's pick the crew called predictable — and the AWP itself. He played drums for four years. He is the twin brother of Reid Hart; the two disagree, good-naturedly, on exactly how many minutes separated their births.

[[player:reid-wrongnumber-hart|Reid "wrongnumber" Hart]] closed Academy with Overpass and the M4A1-S. He took part in three school theater productions, never as the lead. He is the twin brother of Nolan Hart.

The session ended off-script, with Dust2.us asking both rosters a run of quick-fire questions: who sleeps latest, who takes the longest shower, who forgets the most things, who complains about food the most, who has the worst music taste, who would survive alone in a forest, and who would get arrested first on a trip. Glacier was named by four separate teammates as most likely to survive in a forest; RAMENSOUP insisted he could do it too, citing six months as a scout as a child, which p4rkingl0t immediately argued doesn't count.
